name: 1801 Prairie Avenue — W. W. Kimball's Chateauesque house in Bedford stone, built on K01 at the massing J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows (T-2538, moved onto the kit by T-2843; refined by T-2910, T-2911, T-2540, T-1890)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'William W. Kimball Residence. Built 1890'. The Prairie library's other readings run its building to 1892.

research_note: MOVED ONTO K01 BY T-2843 (piece 3 of T-2789), at the massing T-2538 read off J. W. Taylor's photograph of c. 1895 (taylor_c1895_kimball_residence_1801, camera data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/taylor_c1895_northwest.json) and the 1911 sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1801-b1). The draft builder's copy is retired: the house is now an all-stone K01 frontage (T-2788) in Bedford stone, the register's material for it (pa-1801-23): two storeys of wall to a cornice at 8.1 m under steep slate mansard faces to a deck about 16-17 m up; the front's south pavilion and the 18th Street wall's three-storey section on K08 projections carried past the eave to 13.9 m; the round tower on a K08 tower on the 18th Street wall, its cone to about 18.7 m; the gabled section and the east range as slated K01 wings (T-2841). The east range runs the trace's whole length to v 18.3 and carries its north-east corner turret, eaves level with the range's (T-2900); the pavilion's coped gable is not built (T-2540). The corner loggia, its two arches and the swept stair are built (T-2910), and carved as the photograph shows them (T-2923, T-2932); the bowed bay, the front's openings and carving are T-2911's; the roof's dormers, cresting, stacks and the flank's gable are T-2540's; the south wall's two tall stone stacks are T-3107's, read off HABS photograph 1 of June 1965 (habs_kimball_photo_01_sw_1965, camera data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/habs_1965_01_southwest.json), the only picture of the south side; its round south-west corner bay, the south wall's bay, openings and dormers are open in that match record (T-3108, T-3109). T-1890 finishes the architecture. What the build invents is in docs/LIBERTIES.md (L-kimball-1801-k01-2843, after L-kimball-1801-massing-2538) and what differs is open in the match record.

documented_range.note: The record claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building ('3B', stone) and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); J. W. Taylor's photograph shows it standing about 1895. Its building and loss dates are the finishing ticket's to read (T-1890).

stone_front.note: Bedford stone, the register's material for 1801 (frontage register row pa-1801-23, K02's limestone_bedford), laid in smooth courses as the photograph shows on the front and the flank alike, over a two-course base to the basement lights' heads. The front's carved frieze, string courses and corbel table are T-2911's and T-2540's.

street_front_trim.note: The two lights over the loggia, the avenue front's (front_bays 1.6) and the 18th Street flank's (side_bays 18.67), each stand in a moulded frame under a projecting head in the Taylor print (x 1016-1071 and 877-931 px), so the second storey wears the K09 kit's restrained surround, its two-fascia architrave round the light and its cornice hood on consoles, and the flank's light is named in `lights` to wear it too; the print's transom bar stands about 0.75-1.0 m under each head (y 680-700 px at the front, 676-694 on the flank, through T-3074's camera at about 57 px a metre), so each light carries an 0.8 m top light over a 0.1 m bar where K06's transom light is 0.45 m (T-1890). Each light stands between two carved pilasters in the print (front x 1000-1010 and 1075-1085, flank 860-870 and 935-945 px), each rising from the belt under the sill to a carved capital beside the head that carries the head's band, and HABS 1965's photograph 2 shows the 18th Street pair sharply: a sunk-panelled shaft with one lozenge centred on it, about 0.55 m tall and nearly the shaft's width, under a foliate capital. So each named light carries `pilasters` (T-1890): a shaft 0.25 m broad (the Taylor print reads about 0.2 m, 10-11 px at about 50 px a metre on its foreshortened faces; HABS 2 about 0.3 m, its shaft against the light's clear width) and 0.06 m proud, standing 0.1 m clear of the architrave, on a base from the belt's top (5.0 m) under a capital standing where the kit's console hung, the hood run out over the capitals, and one lozenge 0.55 m tall centred on each shaft, carved 0.015 m proud as the bow's are (bays, T-2931). The profiles, the plain capitals (the pictures' are foliate) and the shaft's plain face (HABS 2's is a sunk panel) are the kit's and this reading, not the house's own carving (L-kimball-1801-loggia-lights-1890). The principal storey's openings are the door and the bow's own lights, so its plain stone lintel dresses none on the front.

roof_form.note: Very steep slate faces from the cornice to a deck ringed with cresting about 17 m up, as the photograph shows (T-2538).

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck behind the cresting is not seen from the street; a low hip inside the K05 mansard's upper range.

eave_overhang_m.note: The eave's projection, inside the mansard's range: 0.4 m, so K10's moulded stone cornice (0.32 m out) stands under the soffit inside the fascia (T-3002).

wall_head.note: T-3002: the heavy moulded cornice under the mansard's slate faces in the Taylor photograph, on the avenue front and the 18th Street flank, as K10's moulded stone eave (0.36 m deep, 0.32 m out) under the K05 soffit from 8.34 to 8.7 m, level with the bow's own and dying into the bow, the tower and both pavilions. The section is the kit's generic one; the print's block row under its corona is not built (L-kimball-1801-carved-stone-3002). T-1890: and on the south wall (k01.wall.side.north), where HABS photograph 1 shows the same heavy cornice under the mansard from the round bay at the south-west corner to the south-east corner, carried round the south bay; it starts where the south pavilion's chamfer meets the wall, 1.4 m behind the front, capped against the canted face, and dies into the south bay (L-kimball-1801-south-bay-top-1890). It runs on across the face of the wall gable at that wall's rear corner (p_se_gable, cornice_across), under its lights, to the corner, as HABS photograph 1 shows it (T-1890; L-kimball-1801-gable-cornice-1890).

mansard.note: Read through the solved camera (T-2538): straight steep faces at about 72 degrees from the 8.1 m cornice to a curb 7.2 m higher, so the deck's front edge reads 15.3-16.3 m up, inside the photograph's 15.5-17 m. A face this tall holds the house's third storey and its attic, which is why it passes K05's attic-storey 4.5 m (T-2843 lets a mansard that holds two storeys rise to 7.5 m). The face's two tiers of hooded dormers and the deck's cresting are T-2540's. T-3000: the hooded dormers and the deck read off the same print through T-2538's camera. One hooded dormer shows on each face the camera sees, close by the corner: a short stone face with one small light (about 0.6 by 0.7 m) under a shelf, and over the shelf a tall slated hood with upright cheeks whose front falls about 0.4 m back to a level top (its edge leans about 20 px over the hood's 100), the street's at v 3.0 (the print reads about v 2.7; 3.0 is the nearest a dormer stands to the corner's hip here) its shelf about 10.9 m up, the 18th Street face's at u 16.7 about 0.5 m higher. The deck: a rail of pierced iron cresting about 0.55 m high (about 30 px at 54 px a metre) round the curb, a slated pyramid about 1.0 m across and 1.4 m high rising from the curb's north-west corner under a turned finial, the finials about 2.2 m high. The print shows no second tier of dormers. The dormers' sections, the cresting's pattern and the finials' turnings are reconstructed (L-kimball-1801-deck-cresting-3000). T-3002: on the eave raised to 8.9 m the lower face rises 6.4 m at 69.1 degrees, so the curb stands where the 7.2 m face at 72 degrees put it, and the dormers' faces are set back 0.34 and 0.52 m so their lights keep their heights. T-3109: the south face's hooded dormer between the two stacks, read off HABS photograph 1 through its re-solved camera: its light at x 1072-1120 px, sill y 587 and head y 532 (about 9.8 and 11.1 m), under a tall slated hood whose top stands at y 420 (about 13.6 m), its axis at about u 5.4, its face out at the eave (0.45 m in from the fascia's face) as the print's sits on the cornice. The light's width is not read: the camera foreshortens this face about twice as hard as the print's own courses do, so 0.75 m is the 18th Street dormer's proportion carried to the taller light (L-kimball-1801-south-dormer-3109). T-1890: the three hooded dormers' faces slated as their hoods are, each light in a pale stone frame 0.1 m wide standing 0.04 m out of the slate (hood.face, hood.frame_m), as the Taylor print shows the street and 18th Street dormers' and HABS photograph 1 the south one's; the frame's section is reconstructed (L-kimball-1801-dormer-faces-1890). T-1890: each hood's foot flared 0.2 m wider than its face each side and 0.2 m out in front of it, its shelf with it (hood.flare_m), sweeping in to its top, as HABS photograph 1 shows the south hood's foot about a third wider than its face and HABS photograph 2 and the Taylor print show the other two broad at the foot and standing out of the slate there; the south hood's top eased to 0.81 m across (taper 0.17), as HABS 1 reads it about half its foot (L-kimball-1801-hood-flare-1890). T-1890: the deck stops its cresting at the south pavilion's cross roof, along the front and the south curb, and stands the south-west finial on the cross roof's ridge end, where the Taylor print and HABS photograph 1 both show the finial; the corner carries none of its own (deck.cross_roof, L-kimball-1801-cross-roof-1890).

chimneys.note: T-1890: the flank stack is moved to where both cameras' lines of sight cross, near the main block's north-east corner (u 1.8, v 1.0, within about 10 px of the print's shaft in both: x 611 on HABS photograph 2, x 498 on the Taylor print), where T-3000's u 5.0 rendered about 90 and 50 px west of them; its cap is built to the Taylor print's 16.0 m (HABS 2 reads about 15.5 m; the kit holds a mansard stack 0.6 m over its 15.3 m curb), its shaft 0.9 m square under a 0.3 m cap, in the walls' pale stone as both pictures show it. Its flared bell cap is laid as a slab (within tolerance). L-kimball-1801-flank-top-1890. T-3109: both south stacks dressed as HABS photograph 1 draws them (read on the print, each stack's own width its scale: the front one's 1.2 m shaft spans about 75 px, the rear one's 1.45 m about 68 px). Each stands on a broader base about 0.08 m proud each side, carried up from the cornice and weathered back to the shaft at about 11.85 m (the splay at y 450 px on the front one and about 505 on the rear one, both about 11.8 m through the camera); over the plain shaft a moulded collar (about 22 px, 0.35 and 0.45 m), a stage of diamond lattice (about 60 and 57 px, 1.0 and 1.2 m), two whole diamonds a face of crossed raised ribs, the stage a few centimetres proud of the shaft, and a moulded cap with a dentil course about 0.2 m proud (about 32 and 27 px, 0.5 and 0.55 m). The dentils and the shaft's sunk strips are not modelled (within tolerance). L-kimball-1801-stack-heads-3109. Through T-3108's re-solved camera the front one's cap (its top at y 125 px) reads about 17.8 m, so the 18.0 m the Taylor print allows now fits this picture too, and the rear one's (y 225 px) about 18.5 m, not the 20.1 m T-3107 read through the earlier camera: it is lowered to 18.5 m, still hidden from the Taylor eye behind the north curb. T-3003: the two tall stone stacks of the south wall, read off HABS photograph 1 (Harold Allen, June 1965, from the south-west) through its solved camera (data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/habs_1965_01_southwest.json). Each rises from the main cornice over the south wall, straddling the wall line, in pale ashlar the tone of the walls (not brick), past the deck's cresting to a heavy head; the print's shafts, at x 870-945 and 1122-1190 px of the 1800 px copy, and their caps' tops (y 128 and 210 px), put the front one at u 14.45 about 1.2 m across with its cap at about 19.25 m, the rear one at u 3.2 about 1.45 m across at about 20.1 m. Those heights stand on a camera whose cornice reads low at the corner (see its solve); read against the cresting beside it, at about the same depth, the front one's cap still stands about 167 px (about 3.5 m) over the cresting's top. The Taylor print of c. 1895, the period view the phase guard prefers (T-1890), shows nothing over the deck where that cap would show from its eye: through its camera a cap at u 14.45 clears the build's deck there above about 18.0 m. So the front one is built to 18.0 m, the most the period print allows, and the 1965 height is open in both match records (a stack raised after 1895, or the deck and curb the Taylor record already reads off, T-3108/T-3109); the rear one, 20.1 m, stays hidden from that eye behind the north curb and is built as HABS reads it. T-3000: the flank's tall stone stack, read off the Taylor photograph through T-2538's camera: it rises behind the 18th Street wall at the flank section's east end, about 1.2 m across (x 475-515 px on the print), to about 16.4 m (its cap's top at y 462 px), under a heavy corbelled cap about 0.25 m proud and 0.5 m deep; its depth into the roof is not seen. The pavilion's stack the parent ticket names is not in this print: nothing rises behind the pavilion's gable, and the dark stacks at the print's right edge are 1811's. L-kimball-1801-deck-cresting-3000.

rainwater.note: The kit's copper gutter behind the cornice, its downpipe on the rear wall, which no picture shows; the Taylor photograph shows none on the front. window_kit.note: The district's sash; the plate's sash is too small to count lights. T-3097: the Taylor print's two lights over the loggia (the front's and the 18th Street flank's) each carry a transom bar about 0.7-1.0 m under the head (y 680-700 px at the front, 676-694 on the flank), so the house's sash is K06's one-over-one under a fixed transom (its transom light is the kit's 0.45 m, under the print's); the round-headed pair on the flank (side_bays) is one plate light each, K06's fixed round-headed light, its well left out, where the print draws a bar near each spring that is not built.

entrance_kit.note: T-2910 builds the corner loggia J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows at the front's 18th Street end, read through its solved camera (data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/taylor_c1895_northwest.json): a round arch on the front and one on the 18th Street face, each about 1.9 m across (the front's void x 1010-1095 on the print, v 0.5-2.7; the flank's u 18.1-19.5 inside its surround), centred about 1.6 m from the corner, springing about 2.65 m over grade and crowned about 3.6 m (the photograph's 2.61-2.67 and 3.57), so 2.15 m over the 1.45 m floor; through the 18th Street arch the loggia's back wall and its door frame are seen about on the front arch's axis. Built as K07's deep-arched double door made a loggia: the front arch (opening_m) under its voussoir block, a room 2.3 m square behind it (v 0.45-2.75, 2.75 m behind the front) on the door's floor, the double door in its back wall, and the side arch cut through the 18th Street wall with its own voussoir block, laid in that wall's courses; under the side arch the photograph's stone balcony, its top the arch's sill and its underside corbelled back into the wall. The stair comes down the front out of the arch, as broad as the room, between cheeks whose tops run level by the arch and sweep down in one reversed curve to a block at the foot about 0.85 m over grade (the photograph's left foot block reads 0.68-0.70 m over the walk at the camera's grade, which stands about 0.2 m under the lot's). Reconstructed, and recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kimball-1801-loggia-2910: the room's depth, ceiling and square plan (only its back wall and the door's frame are seen), the door's leaves and transom, the cheeks' thickness, and the balcony's projection and corbel. T-2923 carves both arches' faces as the print shows them: each arch's moulded archivolt, two faces 0.07 and 0.11 m broad stepped 0.035 and 0.07 m out from the intrados, turned round the head and run down both jambs to the floor, with no keystone (the print has none); a carved pier each side 0.22 m outside the intrados and 0.30 m broad (the print's at v 0.1-0.4 and 2.84-3.15 on the front, u 17.0-17.3 and 19.6-20.0 on 18th Street), from the floor on a 0.35 m base to a capital under 3.92 m (the print's capitals at about 3.7-3.95 m), a chain of raised lozenges down each shaft; a rosette in each spandrel, where the print shows carved leafage; a round-headed tablet on each stair foot block's front and two on its outer face; and the balcony's face in four raised panels, each with a lozenge (L-kimball-1801-loggia-carving-2923). T-2932 lays the print's two carved bands over each arch, from capital to capital: the relief frieze from the capitals' 3.92 m to 4.49 m (the print's 3.9-4.5 m), 0.08 m proud and carved with T-2819's guilloche for the print's leafage, under a moulded course to 4.67 m (the print's 4.5-4.7 m); and over it the cartouche band to 5.40 m under the second storey's sill (the print's to about 5.4), 0.06 m proud, an oval cartouche 0.6 m by 0.5 m on the arch's axis and a roundel each side of it for the print's scrolled frames (L-kimball-1801-loggia-frieze-2932). front_yard_m is the 7.7 m from the front to the lot line (street_u 28.2). Graded reconstructed as a whole: its places and sizes are read off the photograph, and what the photograph cannot give is invented within them (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kimball-1801-loggia-2910).
